comments.text:
For those that are interested in this topic, and may have the perception that checks like this will tell you the email will get to the person intended, here is reality.

An email address can be evaluated across multiple independent layers. Each layer increases confidence, but no combination of these checks can definitively prove who will ultimately receive and read the message.

Layer 1: Domain Validation (DNS)
- Does the domain exist?
- Does the domain publish MX records?
- Does the domain publish SPF records?
- Does the domain publish DKIM records?
- Does the domain publish a DMARC policy?
- Is DNSSEC enabled?

These checks establish that the domain is real and configured to send and receive email.

Layer 2: Mail Infrastructure (Network)
- Is the MX server reachable?
- Does it respond to SMTP?
- Does it advertise STARTTLS?
- Is the TLS certificate valid?
- Does reverse DNS (PTR) exist?
- Does forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS) validate correctly?

These checks establish that the mail system is functioning and professionally configured.

Layer 3: Domain Reputation
- Domain age
- Domain expiration date
- Registrar reputation
- Recently registered or transferred
- Suspicious or uncommon TLD
- Presence on known spam or abuse blocklists

Layer 4: Email Address Analysis (Code)

Evaluate the local-part (before the @). Classify whether the address appears to be:

- Generic
- Catch-all
- No-reply
- Functional role (support, sales, billing, accounting)
- Distribution group
- Individual person
- Randomly generated
- High entropy
- Disposable email provider

Layer 5: Organization Validation

- Website exists
- HTTPS configured
- Valid TLS certificate
- Contact information published
- Privacy policy
- Company information
- Public business presence

These checks establish that the email domain appears to belong to a real organization.

Layer 6: Pattern Analysis

- Typosquatting
- Homograph attacks
- Excessive numbers
- Excessive hyphens
- Long randomized domains
- Lookalike brands
- Recently registered impersonation domains

These checks identify domains intentionally designed to deceive.

Layer 7: Optional SMTP Validation

Where supported by the receiving mail server:
- SMTP banner inspection
- EHLO capability analysis
- Recipient validation (if permitted)
- VRFY/EXPN support (rare)
- Open relay detection

These checks provide additional technical confidence without actually sending an email.

The Fundamental Limitation

Even if every validation above succeeds, there is still one question that cannot be answered through technical inspection alone:

Is the person I intend to communicate with actually the person who owns, controls, will receive, and will open this mailbox?

None of these layers can determine:

- Whether the mailbox has changed owners.
- Whether multiple people have access to the mailbox.
- Whether the mailbox is forwarded elsewhere.
- Whether it is monitored by assistants, contractors, or automated systems.
- Whether the intended individual still uses the address.
- Whether the intended recipient is the one who will ultimately read the message.

These validation layers establish confidence in the email infrastructure, the domain, and the address itself. They do not establish confidence in the identity of the human being behind the mailbox.

Ultimately, an email address identifies a mailbox, not a verified person.
